question.prompt:
Positive real numbers \(a\) and \(b\) have the property that

\[ \begin{aligned} &\sqrt{\log a} + \sqrt{\log b} \\ &\quad {}+ \log \sqrt{a} + \log \sqrt{b} = 100 \end{aligned} \]

and all four terms on the left are positive integers, where \(\log\) denotes the base \(10\) logarithm. What is \(ab?\)

solutions.title: Turn logarithms into integers
solutions.explanation:
The integer square-root terms make the logarithms perfect squares, and the other two integer terms force those square roots to be even.

Set
\[
p=\sqrt{\log a},\qquad q=\sqrt{\log b}.
\]
Then \(p,q\) are positive integers, and the logarithm power rule gives
\[
\log\sqrt a=\frac{p^2}{2},\qquad
\log\sqrt b=\frac{q^2}{2}.
\]
Because these are integers, \(p\) and \(q\) must be even: the square of an odd integer is odd. Write \(p=2m\) and \(q=2n\), where \(m,n\) are positive integers. The given equation becomes
\[
2m+2n+2m^2+2n^2=100,
\]
so
\[
m(m+1)+n(n+1)=50.
\]
Neither variable can exceed \(6\), since \(7\cdot8>50\). The complete list of possible summands is

| \(t\) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(t(t+1)\) | 2 | 6 | 12 | 20 | 30 | 42 |

The only two entries that sum to \(50\) are \(20\) and \(30\). Thus \(\{m,n\}=\{4,5\}\), and
\[
\log(ab)=\log a+\log b
=4m^2+4n^2
=4(16+25)=164.
\]
The four original terms are then \(8,10,32,50\), in some order within their respective pairs, and they sum to \(100\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{ab=10^{164}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).

solutions.title: Use odd squares modulo 5
solutions.explanation:
Completing squares turns the condition into a sum of two odd squares, and their remainders modulo \(5\) leave very few possibilities.

Let \(p=\sqrt{\log a}\) and \(q=\sqrt{\log b}\). Both are positive integers. Since
\[
\log\sqrt a=\frac{p^2}{2},\qquad
\log\sqrt b=\frac{q^2}{2}
\]
are also integers, \(p\) and \(q\) are even. Multiplying the original equation by \(2\) and completing squares gives
\[
p^2+2p+q^2+2q=200,
\]
\[
(p+1)^2+(q+1)^2=202.
\]
Put \(u=p+1\) and \(v=q+1\). These are odd integers at least \(3\). Since each square is at most \(202-3^2=193\), each variable belongs to
\[
\{3,5,7,9,11,13\}.
\]
An integer square has remainder \(0,1\), or \(4\) upon division by \(5\): these come from squaring remainders \(0,\pm1,\pm2\). Because \(202\) has remainder \(2\), both \(u^2\) and \(v^2\) must have remainder \(1\), the only way two square remainders can sum to \(2\) modulo \(5\).

Among the six candidates, only \(9\) and \(11\) have squares with remainder \(1\). Moreover,
\[
9^2+11^2=202,
\]
while using either value twice gives \(162\) or \(242\). Consequently \(\{u,v\}=\{9,11\}\), so \(\{p,q\}=\{8,10\}\). Hence
\[
\log(ab)=p^2+q^2=64+100=164,
\]
and
\[
\boxed{ab=10^{164}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
